title: GPU power limit
description: GPU pins to a 285 W board power limit and drops core clock 2640 to 2050 MHz at 68 C, with the vendor reporting a power cap rather than a thermal one.

events.title: GPU power limit
events.whatHappened: Frame time rose to 47 ms while the GPU was limited by a power limit.
events.mechanism: The GPU was drawing as much power as it is allowed to and reduced its clock to stay inside that budget. Less clock means less work per second, so frames take longer. This is the card behaving as designed, not a fault.
events.recommendedAction: This is normal behaviour at stock settings. If the card's power limit is adjustable, raising it trades power and heat for clock. Lowering the graphics settings that drive power draw is the alternative.

evidence.statement: The GPU reported a power limit as the reason for reducing clocks

ruledOut.title: Background CPU contention
ruledOut.reason: Total CPU load did not rise materially (peak 39%).

ruledOut.title: CPU frequency collapse
ruledOut.reason: CPU effective clock stayed near 4.61 GHz.

ruledOut.title: GPU thermal throttling
ruledOut.reason: The GPU reduced clocks for a power limit, not a thermal one.

ruledOut.title: Memory pressure and paging
ruledOut.reason: Hard page faults peaked at 2/s.

ruledOut.title: Storage stall
ruledOut.reason: Disk response time stayed at 0.5 ms.

ruledOut.title: Driver interrupt latency
ruledOut.reason: Kernel-mode time stayed at 0.7% (deferred calls and interrupts).
